standard_prerequisites.name: Colimits of sets and their universal property
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Sets, the description of the colimit of a system of sets by equivalence classes of elements
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that two elements of two different stages become equal in the colimit exactly when they become equal in a later stage, which is the mechanism of the proof.

core_obligations: Surjectivity (proof lines 331-339): a map from a finite set into the colimit has each of its finitely many values represented in some stage, and since the system is directed one stage contains representatives of all of them, which exhibits the map as coming from that stage.

Injectivity (proof lines 340-345): two maps from the finite set into a single stage that agree in the colimit agree on each of the finitely many elements after passing to a later stage, and again directedness gives a single stage where the two maps agree, which is injectivity.
proof_roadmap: Realise the finitely many values of a map into the colimit at a single stage for surjectivity.
For injectivity, use that agreement in the colimit happens at a later stage for each element.
Combine the finitely many stages into one by directedness.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the comparison map of an inductive system of sets is a bijection when tested against a finite set (statement lines 325-329). The proof is a complete argument: surjectivity follows because the finitely many values of a map into the colimit are represented in a single stage by directedness (proof lines 331-339); injectivity follows because two maps agreeing in the colimit agree at each of the finitely many elements after passing to a later stage, and the finitely many stages can be combined into one (proof lines 340-345). The non-formal content is the finite bookkeeping with directedness. The claim is H2.
